{{Quote|Before you lie the ruins of the temple of the Sith. You stand on the threshold of power, amid the bones of defilers and tomb robbers.|Freedon Nadd|audio=NaddThreshold-DLotS.flac|<ref name="Tales of the Jedi: Dark Lords of the Sith (audio)" />}}
The '''Great Temple''' was a mausoleum as well as a place of reverence located in [[Korriban/Legends|Korriban's]] [[Valley of the Dark Lords/Legends|Valley of the Dark Lords]], where the remains of many of the most honored [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lords of the Sith]] were interred.

==Description==
A massive structure built of stone by the [[Sith (species)/Legends|Sith]], the Great Temple was one of the most prominent structures within the [[Valley of the Dark Lords/Legends|Valley of the Dark Lords]] on [[Korriban/Legends|Korriban]], and situated at the very rear of the valley itself. Towering over other structures, the [[Hall of Judgment (Korriban)|Hall of Judgment]] held the bodies of many [[Death/Legends|deceased]] [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lords]], all of which remained untouched by time, preserved by their own power in the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side of the Force]]. [[Tuk'ata/Legends|Tuk'ata]] hounds prowled the interior of the temple, and served as guardians against tomb-raiders and grave-robbers. The walls of a Sith mausoleum were covered in the [[Massassi (alphabet)|Massassi]] inscriptions.<ref name="TOTJ3" />

==History==
===Krath Holy Crusade===
{{Quote|Take refuge in the ''Great Temple''--I will ''protect'' you!|Freedon Nadd, to Exar Kun|<ref name="TOTJ3" />}}
[[File:Exar_Kun_reading_Sith.png|thumb|right|250px|Exar Kun reading Sith hieroglyphs on a throne in the Great Temple.]]
In [[3997 BBY]],<ref name="NEC">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''</ref> [[Padawan/Legends|Jedi apprentice]] [[Exar Kun/Legends|Exar Kun]] was guided to Korriban and into the Great Temple by the [[Force ghost/Legends|spirit]] of [[Freedon Nadd]]. After several tests, Nadd tricked Kun into finally embracing [[The Force/Legends|the Force's]] dark side after the destruction of the [[great crystal]] brought a deadly avalanche of stone down on Kun's head.<ref name="TOTJ3" />

===Sith Empire===
The Temple would be forgotten for millennia after Kun's visit and, while the [[Sith Empire/Legends|Sith Empire]] would occasionally hold the planet, its [[Sith Academy (Korriban)|Sith Academy]] was erected in front of the Temple complex as the above-ground portions of the Great Temple became largely uninhabitable and continued to collapse.

===Galactic Republic===
In [[23 BBY/Legends|23 BBY]], a team of Jedi Knights and their [[Padawan/Legends|Padawans]], headed by [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]], entered the Great Temple while on a [[Mission to Korriban (23 BBY)|mission]] to track down the galactic criminals [[Granta Omega]] and [[Jenna Zan Arbor]]. Upon entering the ancient ruins, Kenobi felt a distinct Sith presence—the dark shape of a Sith Lord. Though he did not realize it at the time, this later proved to have been [[Dooku/Legends|Darth Tyranus]], the Sith alter-ego of former [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] Dooku, who was there on Korriban to rendezvous with Omega and Zan Arbor. The two criminals were seeking to strike an alliance of power with the galaxy's re-emergent Sith. [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]] had fleetingly glimpsed the tall, black-hooded figure of the Sith Lord from behind. Kenobi shuddered at the thought of the thousands, who had come for knowledge and training, who had been trapped within the Sith Temple by their own desires: he seemed to feel each wasted life, each terrible death. So thick and foreboding was the dark side of the Force within the Temple, that it seemed to invade Kenobi's lungs, and he found it difficult to breathe. For 18-year-old Anakin, the surging feeling of the dark side seemed to rise up from the soles of his feet and blast through the crown of his head: its undeniable power was stomach-turning, nerve-splitting—nauseating.<ref name=":0">''[[Jedi Quest: The Final Showdown]]''</ref>

===Galactic Empire and New Republic===
{{Quote|Emperor of numberless worlds... ''Lord Vader's'' throne still remains empty. Have you now come to take his place and ''join us''?&hellip; The doomed flesh you wear has yielded to ''necrosis''. This clone body ''cannot'' be saved.|The Dark Lord of the Sith, to Palpatine|<ref name="EE 2" />}}
[[File:VadersThrone-EE2P5.jpg|thumb|left|250px|An ancient Dark Lord offering Vader's throne to Palpatine.]]
The Temple would once more be explored by [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]] during the reign of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]]. A [[Tomb of Darth Vader|throne]] was prepared for Darth Vader within the Temple; Vader would never occupy it<ref name="EE 2" /> as he died embracing his [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] heritage on the [[Endor/Legends|forest moon]] of [[Endor (planet)/Legends|Endor]].<ref name="ROTJ">{{Film|VI}}</ref> In [[11 ABY/Legends|11 ABY]],<ref name="NEC" /> the reborn Palpatine visited the Great Temple seeking counsel from the spirits of his [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] predecessors in order to restore his decaying clone body. As they traveled through the ancient Sith crypt, the [[Dark side adept/Legends|Dark Side Adept]] [[T'iaz]] felt the dark side power emanating from the place. Palpatine explained to him that<ref name="EE 2" /> the ancient Dark Lords<ref name="EE audio">[[Empire's End (audio drama)|''Empire's End'' audio drama]]</ref> were preserved by the very [[Sith alchemy/Legends|Sith alchemy]] that made them [[Exiles|outcasts]]. [[Unidentified Dark Lord (Great Temple)|One Dark Lord]] doubted his success and offered him Vader's throne, but Palpatine declined and instead demanded to be healed. The spirit suggested Palpatine to gaze into the [[oracle stone]], through which Palpatine learned that the only way for him to survive would to to [[Essence transfer|transfer his spirit]] into [[Anakin Solo]], the newborn son of [[Princess/Legends|Princess]] [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa Solo]]. The other spirits gave Palpatine counsel and bid him farewell a final time.<ref name="EE 2">[[Empire's End 2|''Empire's End'' 2]]</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|tying the Emperor's incapcitated state and shortage of clones in SW Missions: Vader's Return with the trip to Korriban shortly after Yavin mentioned in Empire's End #2|[[Abel G. Peña]]|<ref name="jcf">{{JCFCite|url=posts/3425564|board=Literature|thread=The Emperor's Pawns article (was: Gamer #5 stuff @ TOS!!!)|user=[[Abel G. Peña|Halagad_Ventor]]|date=2001-07-16|time=9:22 PM|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20200420171538/https://boards.theforce.net/threads/the-emperors-pawns-article-was-gamer-5-stuff-tos.3223225/page-4#post-3425564}}</ref>}}
The article ''[[The Emperor's Pawns]]'', published in [[2001]]'s [[Star Wars Gamer 5|''Star Wars Gamer'' 5]] and written by [[Abel G. Peña]] and [[Juan Schwartz]], expanded on Palpatine's visit to Korriban shortly after the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]] mentioned in the [[1995]] [[Star Wars comic books|comic book]] [[Empire's End 2|''Empire's End'' 2]]. It is said that he "enraged the mummified Sith by demanding dark side knowledge."<ref name="TEP">{{GamerCite|5|The Emperor's Pawns}}</ref> It is unclear whether the mummified Sith mentioned are meant to be the Dark Lords in the Great Temple from ''Empire's End'' 2.

The Great Temple with its [[Sith Academy (Korriban)|Sith Academy]] on Korriban is referenced in the [[Jedi Quest: The Final Showdown|final volume]] of [[Jude Watson]]'s ''[[Star Wars: Jedi Quest|Jedi Quest]] ''series simply as the "ancient Sith monastery"—thousands of years old, deserted for hundreds of years, but still a presence of evil. Once a bastion of Sith lore and learning where thousands had once trained "and thousands of hopefuls had once disappeared forever," the Temple was, at once, repulsive ''and'' alluring to the Jedi. The original inhabitants of Korriban who had built (and, in later years, ''re-built'') the Sith complex had, of course, long since vanished and nothing thrived there: but if the ancient stones could speak, "they would talk of blood and terror." For though the Temple had had the same goals as did the [[Jedi Temple/Legends|Jedi Temple]]—''study'' and ''learning''—this place had been ruled by ''fear''. The high walls that narrowed in harsh lines and pyramidal angles near the top were designed to create a feeling of entrapment; slightly askew, they were meant to intimidate and keep beings off-balance. With no openings to light or air, there were only the massive columns, bleak towering walls, and hard floors of cold gray stone.<ref name=":0" />

Watson describes the massive Temple structures as having giant exterior walls comprised of great stones that, by [[23 BBY/Legends|23 BBY]], had "shifted" over the years, with sundry large slabs propped up against one another, and others that had toppled and crumbled into boulders; within, vast echoing chambers that rivaled the Jedi Temple's [[Great Hall (Naboo)/Legends|Great Hall]] were shrouded in darkness. An oppressive dread emanated from the ancient cracks and hollows; the walls wept with moisture. Ancient voices could be heard, and spectral images of torture and pain passed, then vanished, like phantoms in the night. In Watson's description, huge statues of terrifying beasts from many worlds marched on either sides of its great corridors. Vestiges of the Sith's greed-torn Order were strewn across a vast, ancient hangar where aggression and technology met—remains of huge hulking ships were witnesses to the Order's own perceived invincibility that, ultimately, was brought down in disaster by vengeance, lust and pride.<ref name=":0" />
